title: COP1 is a temperature-responsive switch in Arabidopsis
title_zh: COP1 是拟南芥中的温度响应开关
abstract: Temperature is molecular motion, but how living systems sense this is poorly understood. Many responses in plants integrate light and temperature signals, for example, via light receptors and the circadian clock. CONSTITUTIVE PHOTOMORPHOGENESIS 1 (COP1) regulates light signaling and is necessary for responding to temperature. We show that COP1 acts as a temperature-dependent switch, becoming activated by a warm temperature-induced conformational change. An intramolecular Val-Pro (VP) motif binds to the active site of COP1 at low temperatures, preventing substrate docking. At warmer temperatures, the VP motif becomes detached, enabling client proteins to bind and be degraded. This discovery explains how plants are able to obtain a precise readout of temperature within a given climate range. Altering the binding of the VP motif is sufficient to adjust the temperature range within which the plant responds. This helps us understand how plants are able to adapt to different climates.
abstract_zh: 温度是分子运动，但生物体如何感知温度尚不清楚。许多植物反应整合光和温度信号，例如通过光受体和昼夜节律。CONSTITUTIVE PHOTOMORPHOGENESIS 1（COP1）调控光信号，且对温度响应必不可少。我们表明 COP1 是一个温度依赖的开关，由温度诱导的构象变化激活。一个分子内的 Val-Pro（VP）motif 在低温时结合到 COP1 的活性位点，阻止底物结合。在较高温度下，VP motif 脱离，使客户蛋白能够结合并被降解。这一发现解释了植物如何在给定气候范围内获得精确的温度读数。改变 VP motif 的结合足以调整植物响应的温度范围。这有助于我们理解植物如何适应不同气候。
